guides.title: Declare CMS resources as data
guides.summary: defineResource() declares fields, indexes, access rules, ownership and explicit migration steps; the planner turns declarations into additive RomeDB DDL.
guides.markdown:
A resource is plain data, so it can live in application code or a plugin manifest. Field builders map to one RomeDB field type and CHECK each: `string`, `text`, `enum`, `integer`, `bigint`, `number`, `boolean`, `datetime` (Unix milliseconds), `reference`, `json`, `list`, `vector` and `blocks`; `field.slug(from)`, `field.terms(taxonomy)` and `field.media()` build a unique slug derived from another field, indexed term IDs and a media file ID. Options include `required`, `nullable`, `default`, `max`, `min`, `pattern`, `unique`, `index` and `search` (full-text). Records are stored in a strict collection `r__<owner>__<name>` with host fields for revision, operation, timestamps and owner. `schemaless: true` types only the host fields in the database and validates the rest in the host, so field changes need no DDL; collections use it.

Access rules per action are `public`, `authenticated`, `owner` (needs `ownership: true`), `{ permission }`, `{ where: { field: value } }` (records whose fields match, such as published posts), `{ any: [...] }` or `none`. Unlisted actions require `<resource>:<action>`, for example `app/tickets:update`. Field `access` hides or locks single fields.

`cms.plan()` reads the live catalog through INFO and plans additive DDL: new collections, optional fields and indexes. A changed type, a new required field or a tighter rule is blocked until an explicit step covers it: `backfill`, `tighten`, `rename` (keep the old field declared) and, in a later release, `drop`. `cms.migrate()` applies each step as one atomic batch with `ifSequence` from the planning read, records it in the `cms_migrations` ledger with the exact RomeQL and engine release, and re-plans when another write lands first. A failed step rolls back and its resource stays inactive.

guides.title: Read and write records through repositories
guides.summary: Repositories authorize every call, compile bounded parameterized RomeQL, and write the record, revision, audit row and outbox event in one atomic batch.
guides.markdown:
`createCMS({ db, modules, resources, plugins, storage })` builds the host; `cms.resource(id)` returns a repository with `get`, `list`, `count`, `countMany`, `search` (full-text over `search: true` fields), `create`, `update`, `delete` and `revisions`. `where` takes a value, `{ ne }`, `{ in }`, ranges (`gt`, `gte`, `lt`, `lte`) and, on indexed lists such as terms, `{ contains }` or `{ containsAny }`; `order` and `offset` give numbered pages, `after` cursor pages. Empty slug fields are derived from their source field, and taken slugs get `-2`, `-3`, …. Every call takes the request principal. Owner rules become query conditions, and owner-scoped search computes allowed IDs first and checks every hit again in the same query. Public shapes are JSON-safe: `{ id, rev, createdAt, updatedAt, owner, ...fields }`, with bigint fields as decimal strings.

A mutation is one atomic batch. An edit carries `expectedRevision`; a stale revision, lost access or a concurrent edit of the same record fails with `CMS_CONFLICT` and writes nothing else, because the revision, audit and outbox rows are guarded by the operation ID the record statement wrote. Before the batch, `cms.resource.before-write` filters can adjust or reject the draft under a deadline. After commit, `cms.outbox.dispatch()` delivers `cms.resource.after-commit` events and retries only the plugins that failed. An unconfirmed write fails with `CMS_UNCERTAIN` and is completed by `db.recoverPending()`.

guides.title: Define collections, blocks, taxonomies, settings and media
guides.summary: Collections are content types defined as data and stored schemaless; blocks fields hold typed content blocks; taxonomies group entries by nested terms; settings and media are host services.
guides.markdown:
A collection, such as `products`, is the resource `cms/<name>` built from a `CollectionDefinition`: label, title, generated slug, publishing (draft, pending review, scheduled, published, trash), nesting through `parent`, taxonomies, a public URL `path` and fields. A `path` of `''` serves entries at the site root, as WordPress's "Post name" permalinks do: root entries share one slug namespace with other root collections, archive bases and the application's `reservedPaths`, and `cms.archiveUrl(collection)` finds where a root collection's archive lives (for posts, the Reading settings' posts page). Posts and pages are built-in collections in `contentModule`; administrators add collections and fields with `cms.saveCollection(definition, principal)`, which needs `cms:collections`. Each collection is its own document table without `STRICT`: saving changes only indexes and records the declaration hash with the stored definition in one step. Built-in collections keep their core fields and accept added ones; their `fieldOrder` places the module's fields among the added ones, and new fields go last. Every collection also has `seo` (a `field.group()` of title, description, social image, canonical URL and noindex), `locale` and `translationGroup`; one with `comments: true` has `commentsOpen`. When a package upgrade changes a built-in collection or adds host tables, `ready()` applies them on the next request. Hosts call `await cms.ready()` per request to load definitions; a write that finds a newer definition reloads it first.

A `blocks` field holds a tree of `{ id, type, data }`: a container's `children` hold more blocks, and every block may carry a `layout` (`hide`: the container widths `sm`, `md`, `lg` it is hidden at), which core checks. `CORE_BLOCKS` are paragraph, heading, image, gallery, quote, list, code, button, embed, divider and the layout blocks `core/group` (a stack with a width), `core/columns` (holding only `core/column`, which has a `span` out of 12) and `core/grid` (columns per width); plugins add types in their manifest's `blocks`, and a type declares `children: { allowed?, max? }` to hold blocks and `parent` to go only inside those types. A block type names a Solar `icon` and a `category` from `BLOCK_CATEGORIES` (text, media, design, widgets, embeds; default widgets), which the editor's block picker groups by. The host validates every block's data against its type on write, and the tree against the types' rules: at most 200 blocks and 4 levels per field, IDs distinct across the tree. `validateBlocks`, `blockMedia`, the revision diff and patterns walk the tree; `flattenBlocks`, `placeBlocks`, `findBlock`, `updateBlock`, `insertBlock`, `moveBlock`, `shiftBlock` (up, down, in, out) and `blockTreeProblem` are the tree helpers editors use. A required text field must not be blank.

Every block may also carry a `style`: slugs of the active theme's presets for `background`, `text`, `padding`, `margin` and `fontSize`, plus `align` (left, center, right); `layout` adds `anchor` (an HTML id) and `className`. A type's `supports` (`color`, `spacing`, `typography`: true, false or a list of properties) narrows or widens its category's defaults (`blockSupports`: text blocks get all three, media blocks spacing alone, the rest colour and spacing); `validateBlocks` keeps the supported properties and drops the rest. A theme's manifest declares `presets` (`colors`, `fontSizes`, `spacing` as `{ slug, name, value }`, checked by `presetProblems`; `DEFAULT_PRESETS` fills missing kinds and a child theme's layer over its parent's by slug); the site's changes live in the `appearance.presets` setting keyed by theme (`presetOverridesProblem`) and `resolvePresets` combines them. `blockStyleAttributes(block)` gives a styled block's wrapper (`cms-block cms-bg-<slug> …`, inline `background-color: var(--cms-color-<slug>)`, the anchor as `id`), `presetStyle(presets)` the custom properties for the content root, and `customCssProblem` checks the `appearance.customCss` setting (no `@import`, `url()`, scripts or tags).

`cms.taxonomies` keeps terms with a materialized path of ancestor IDs: `create`, `update` (a move rewrites the subtree in one statement), `delete` (children move up), `tree`, `subtree`, `ancestors`, `counts` and `ensure` (tags typed by name). Records hold term IDs in indexed arrays, so `{ containsAny: await cms.taxonomies.subtree(id) }` lists a category and the categories below it. `cms.saveTaxonomy()` adds vocabularies.

`cms.settings` stores validated groups (General, Media, Writing, Reading and those modules add), cached per isolate. `cms.files` (with `storage`) accepts uploads whose declared type matches the file signature, records image size, alt text and captions, and lists the library by kind.

guides.title: Build themes, menus and rich text content
guides.summary: Themes are plugins with site templates and options; menus are revisioned trees resolved for visitors; rich text fields store validated ProseMirror JSON rendered to escaped HTML.
guides.markdown:
Themes are plugins, as extensions are in VS Code. A plugin manifest's `theme` field declares the label, menu `locations` (such as `primary` and `footer`) and `options`, settings fields shown under Appearance → Customize and stored as `<plugin>.<option>`. The plugin ships its templates as files under `templates/`, one default export each: `layout.ts`, `entry.ts` and `archive.ts`, optional `home.ts`, `search.ts` and `not-found.ts`, and narrower ones picked at render time: `entry-<collection>.ts`, `archive-<collection>.ts`, `term.ts` and `term-<taxonomy>.ts`. A `ui.ts` `theme` export (a `SiteTheme`, with `templates` for the narrower ones and `blocks` overrides) is also accepted and wins slot by slot; `assembleSiteTheme(registration)` builds the theme, `entryTemplate` and `archiveTemplate` pick one for a view. Themes own templates, never routes: a route a theme needs is an ordinary plugin page. `templates/head.ts` returns a `HeadValue` (stylesheets and fonts from the plugin's `assets/`, linked with `helpers.asset('assets/theme.css')`), merged under the page's own head. A theme's `server.ts` exports `loaders` (`ThemeLoaders`) keyed like templates; the site runs `layout` and the one loader the template hierarchy picks, with the plugin's grants, the visitor principal and a time limit, and templates read the plain JSON as `helpers.data.layout` and `helpers.data.page` (empty before the grant or on failure). `EntryView.fields` holds every field's typed value (media as `MediaView`, references as `{ id, title, url }`, terms as links). Site collections get a core `template` field: editors choose one of the active theme's `entry-*` templates (`cms.entryTemplates()`). `theme.extends` names a parent theme whose templates, loaders, assets, options, locations and areas the child layers over (one level). `theme.areas` declares widget areas, edited under Appearance → Widgets (`cms.areas`, `cms.areaLocations()`) and rendered on `SiteView.areas`. A manifest's `collections` ship site collections with the plugin, shown only while it is active. Editors edit an entry's blocks and body on the public page with `?edit`: `helpers.block` and `helpers.content` mark them in edit mode, so a theme that renders blocks through the helpers is editable. `helpers.block` renders a container's children through itself and wraps a hidden block in a `data-hide` marker; the scaffold's `cms/blocks.css` lays out groups, columns and grids with CSS grid and `@container` queries against the content root (`.cms-content`, which site pages wrap the theme's page in and a theme puts around a widget area), so the site editor's device toggle only narrows that root. Themes override the classes in their stylesheet or a container's renderer in `blocks`. A styled block (its `style` and `layout.anchor` or `className`) renders inside one `div.cms-block` wrapper with classes per property and the presets' variables inline; the manifest's `theme.presets` (colours, font sizes, spacing) layer over a parent theme's and over the core defaults, Appearance → Customize changes palette values, adds colours and site-level Additional CSS (`appearance.presets`, `appearance.customCss`), and `helpers.presets` holds the result, which `siteContent` puts on the content root as custom properties and a theme's layout can put on its root with `presetStyle`. Templates get plain views (`SiteView`, `EntryView`, `ArchiveView`, resolved `MenuItemView` trees) and `ThemeHelpers` (`options`, `presets`, `content(parts)`, `block(block)`, `isActive(url)`); they never read the database. `cms.themes()` lists them with their `problems`, `cms.activeTheme()` resolves the `appearance.theme` setting to a usable theme, and `cms.activateTheme(name, principal)` switches it at runtime. Theme templates need no grant; a theme's resources, hooks and network access follow the plugin grant. `cossack add cms` renders `src/plugins/default-theme/` as application source. A manifest's `logo` and `cover` name images in the plugin's `assets/` (default `assets/logo.*` and `assets/cover.*`); the Plugins and Themes screens show them, or initials and a gradient when a plugin ships none. A plugin that only ships a theme has nothing to grant and counts as active.

`cms.menus` stores each menu's items as one JSON tree with a revision: `create`, `update(id, { name, items }, { principal, expectedRevision })` (a stale revision is `CMS_CONFLICT` and writes nothing), `delete`, `place(id, locations)`, `assign(location, id | null)` and `forLocation(location)`, which resolves entries and terms by ID to their current titles and URLs for visitors, hides unpublished or deleted targets and is cached per isolate. Items are `link`, `entry`, `archive` or `term`; `menuProblems` validates them (300 items, 5 levels). The editor works on rows: `flattenMenu`, `buildMenu`, `moveRows`, `dropDepths` and `shiftRows` implement drag-and-drop and the move buttons. All of this needs `cms:appearance`.

A `field.richText()` field stores a ProseMirror (TipTap) document, `{ type: 'doc', content }`. `checkRichText` and the repository accept only the declared nodes, marks and attributes, with safe link and image URLs; top-level `cmsBlock` nodes embed blocks validated like a blocks field. `richTextHtml` renders escaped HTML, `richTextParts` splits a document at its blocks for themes, `richTextPlain` and `richTextExcerpt` give its text. A searchable rich text or blocks field indexes its plain text, kept in `_text_<field>`. Posts and pages have a `content` blocks field; the `core/richtext` block is the word processor among the blocks, and a collection's `template` (with `templateLock`) is the blocks every new entry starts with. Blocks of the `data` category (`core/meta`) store values and render nothing.

guides.title: Write a CMS plugin within its manifest
guides.summary: A plugin's manifest declares resources, hooks, permissions, network hosts, slots and commands; its server.ts registers handlers through a context limited to those declarations.
guides.markdown:
`cossack add plugin` renders a plugin package into `src/plugins/<name>/`. The manifest (`plugin.json`) declares `resources`, `blocks` (block types named `<plugin>/<name>`), `hooks` (extension points and versions), `permissions.resources` (access to resources the plugin does not own), `permissions.network` (hosts), `permissions.define` (new permissions), `ui.slots` links and `commands`. `server.ts` exports `register(context)`: `context.hooks` accepts only declared extension points, `context.commands.add` only declared commands, `context.cms` reaches only the plugin's resources and granted ones, and `context.fetch` only granted hosts. Plugin pages under `src/plugins/<name>/pages` route like application pages; pages under `pages/dashboard/` share the dashboard layout. They use `c.get('cms').pluginCms('<name>')`. `ui.ts` can export `slots` with components for `dashboard.overview`, and `blocks` with a component per block type, which the site renders with `{ block }`. Extension points: `cms.resource.before-write` and `after-commit`, the form hooks (`cms.form.*`), `cms.term.before-save`, `cms.comment.before-save` (return `status: 'spam'` to hold a comment) and `cms.menu.before-save`, and the dashboard list filters `cms.dashboard.entry-actions`, `entry-columns` and `bulk-actions`, whose actions are links or plugin commands run with `{ resource, id }` or `{ resource, ids }`.

A plugin runs only when its schema is migrated and an administrator grants what the manifest requests (`/dashboard/plugins`); an upgrade that requests more needs a new grant, and disabling removes the grants. Builds of CMS applications run the plugin policy lints (`cossack plugins check`): raw RomeQL, the RomeDB client, undeclared network hosts, permissions, resources or hooks, and host secrets fail the build. `cossack <plugin>:<command>` runs a command in the application as a signed-in dashboard user.

guides.title: Use CMS auth, sessions and ledgers
guides.summary: The scaffolded src/auth.ts runs @cossackframework/auth on CMS users and RomeDB sessions; createCmsAuth() does the same for hand-written apps, and the host provides the session bag and ledgers.
guides.markdown:
With the `cms` feature, the scaffold renders the shared `auth` and `dashboard` pages over CMS storage: `src/auth.ts` exports the same functions as the database variant (`loginUser`, `registerUser`, `requestPasswordReset`, `resetPassword`, `listUserSessions`, …), backed by `cms.users` and `cms.authSessions`. Starting a session records the user's `lastSignInAt`, which outlives the session; `sessionsOf`, `revokeSessionOf` and `revokeSessionsOf` serve the user screen's Sessions tab, and `createApiToken`, `listApiTokens` and `revokeApiToken` its Application passwords tab; only the user and administrators see them (`canManageAccess`). An application password acts as its user, so give an integration its own user with a narrow role. Registration follows the General settings' "Anyone can register" and default role; reset tokens are stored as SHA-256 hashes and one request can use each.

`createCmsAuth(cms)` returns the auth middleware, a session manager on the `cms_auth_sessions` table (keyed by token, so rotation is one conditional update and exactly one concurrent rotation wins), `signIn`, `signOut`, a realtime descriptor provider whose public reference survives rotation while the fingerprint does not, and `principal(c)` for the request. Users and roles live in relational tables; `cms.users` creates, lists, searches, updates and deletes users, manages roles, verifies passwords with `@cossackframework/auth`'s hasher and resolves roles into a principal. `DEFAULT_ROLES` are Administrator, Editor, Author and Subscriber.

`cms.sessions` is the framework session bag with one row per key, so concurrent writes to different keys never overwrite each other. `cms.oauthStates` consumes OAuth state with one conditional delete. `cms.jobs()` and `cms.notifications()` are the core RomeQL ledgers on RomeDB. `FileService` keeps bytes in Cossack object storage and ownership in RomeDB, with a `sweep()` that finishes or cleans up interrupted uploads and deletes.

`cms:users` manages accounts and `cms:roles` defines roles and chooses users' roles; the dashboard lets a user manager without `cms:roles` add users only with the default role and keeps accounts that can manage roles out of its reach. `cms.uploadAvatar(userId, file, { principal })` stores a still or animated profile picture (PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP, AVIF; 5 MB) in the media library for the user themself or a user manager, sets it on the user and returns its URL.

guides.title: Schedule, preview, revise, redirect, translate and moderate CMS content
guides.summary: Scheduled entries and maintenance publishing, preview links, autosaves, revision restore and diffs, automatic and managed redirects, application passwords, signed webhooks, comments, patterns, languages and image variants on the CMS host.
guides.markdown:
**Scheduling.** Saving `published` with a future `publishedAt` stores `scheduled`; `cms.publishDue()` (run by maintenance every minute) publishes due entries as `system:scheduler`, so outbox events and webhooks fire then. `pending` means pending review. Visitors read `published` only.

**Previews and autosave.** `cms.createPreviewLink(resource, id, principal)` returns a 7-day token stored as its SHA-256; `cms.previewByToken(token)` reads the entry whatever its status, and `revokePreviewLinks` ends them. `cms.autosave(resource, id | 'new', principal, values)`, `latestAutosave` and `discardAutosave` keep one autosave per user and entry.

**Revisions.** `repository.revision(id, n)`, `repository.restore(id, n, { expectedRevision })` (keeps status, publication time, slug, nesting and language) and `compareRecords(fields, before, after)` / `diffWords(a, b)` for word-level diffs.

**Redirects.** When a published entry's URL changes, the update's batch records a 301 from the old URL, retargets redirects to it and drops one from the new URL; path changes of collections and taxonomies add prefix redirects (`/old/*` to `/new/*`). `cms.redirects.match(path)` serves paths without content; `save`, `list`, `delete` and `hit` manage them. Statuses: 301, 302, 307, 308 and 410.

**API and webhooks.** `cms.apiTokens.create(userId, { name, scope })` returns `cms_<id>.<secret>` once; `cms.tokenPrincipal(token)` resolves it (read-only tokens may only GET). `cms.webhooks.save({ name, url, events, collections })` subscribes to `entry.created`, `entry.updated`, `entry.published`, `entry.unpublished` and `entry.deleted`; deliveries are queued from the outbox and sent by `cms.webhooks.dispatch()` with `X-Cossack-Signature: sha256=` HMAC of `<timestamp>.<body>` (check with `verifyWebhookSignature`), retried over six attempts.

**Comments.** `cms.postComment(input, { principal, ip })` applies Settings → Discussion (sign-in, name and email, closing after N days, thread depth, moderation of all or first-time commenters, links, disallowed words) and a 15-second throttle per address; `cms.moderateComments(ids, status | 'delete', principal)` needs `cms:comments`.

**Patterns and languages.** The built-in `patterns` collection holds reusable blocks; a `core/pattern` block references a synced one. `cms.saveLanguages({ default, others }, principal)` sets the site's languages; other languages' URLs get a `/<code>` prefix from `entryUrls`, `cms.translations(collection, record)` maps languages to entries and `cms.translateEntry(collection, id, locale, principal)` starts a draft translation.

**Images.** Pass `images: ImageTransformer` (the Images binding on Workers, sharp on Node) to `createCMS`; `cms.files.variant(id, { width, height, accept })` makes and keeps resized AVIF/WebP variants, `setEdits(id, { crop, focus })` crops and sets the focal point, and `imageSrcset(file)` lists variants for `srcset`.

**Sign-in security.** `cms.security` keeps authenticator secrets (`startTotp`, `confirmTotp`, `verifyCode`), recovery codes, passkeys and short-lived challenges for pending sign-ins.

guides.title: Build forms from blocks and handle their submissions
guides.summary: The forms collection, input blocks with conditional logic, per-form submission tables, cms.forms.submit with spam checks and validation hooks, notifications with merge tags, webhooks, and handling and exporting submissions.
guides.markdown:
**Model.** A form is an entry of the built-in `forms` collection (`formsModule`): `title`, `slug` (names the form on the site and in the API), `enabled`, `body` (a blocks field with `form: true`), `settings` (`FORM_SETTINGS`: submit label, a Markdown message or a redirect, closed message, `limit`, `opensAt`, `closesAt`, `requireSignIn`, `oncePerUser`, `oncePerEmail`, `store`, `recordIp`, `turnstile`) and `notifications` (`{ rules: NotificationRule[] }`, at most 10). Inputs are blocks whose declaration has `input: { kind }` (`string`, `text`, `email`, `url`, `phone`, `number`, `boolean`, `date`, `choice`, `choices`); `FORM_BLOCKS` ships `form/text`, `form/email`, `form/url`, `form/phone`, `form/textarea`, `form/number`, `form/date`, `form/select`, `form/radio`, `form/checkboxes`, `form/checkbox`, `form/consent` and `form/hidden`. Plugins build their own with `inputFields(own)`. Input blocks go only in a `form: true` field; an input without `name` takes one from its label in camel case. Containers lay inputs out. Any block in a form can carry `when: { action?, match?, rules: [{ field, op, value? }] }` with `is`, `isNot`, `contains`, `empty`, `notEmpty`, `gt`, `lt` and `in`; `formVisibility` evaluates it, hidden inputs counting as empty. `validateSubmission(blocks, types, raw)` reads posted values by kind, applies conditions and checks the shown inputs; the browser and the host run the same code.

**Storage.** Each form's submissions are a schemaless resource `cms/form_<form id>` (`submissionResource`) in their own table `r__cms__form_<id>`, never a shared one: one field per input, plus `status` (`new`, `read`, `spam`, `trash`), `note` and `meta` (`ip`, `userAgent`, `referrer`, `page`, `locale`); the sender is `owner`. `cms.forms` keeps the table in step with the form's inputs (additive) and drops it when the form is deleted. Handling needs `cms:submissions` (Editors by default).

**Submitting.** `cms.forms.submit(slugOrId, raw, { principal, ip, userAgent, page, origin, trap, startedAt, botCheck })` checks the schedule, the limit (kept submissions), sign-in, the bot check, one post per address and form every five seconds, then `validateSubmission`, `cms.form.validate` (add errors), `cms.form.before-submit` (change values) and the once rules. The trap field or a post within two seconds of rendering is kept as `spam` and answered as usual. One batch writes the record, a receipt and a `form.submitted` outbox event; `store: false` writes the event alone. The answer is `{ form, submission, confirmation }` after `cms.form.confirmation`; merge tags in the message are filled with Markdown-escaped answers.

**After a submission.** The outbox runs `cms.form.submitted` (`FormSubmittedEvent`, key work on `eventId`): the host sends each notification rule through `createCMS({ mail, mailFrom })` once per event, rule and address, after `cms.form.notification` (return null to skip), and queues `form.submitted` webhooks. Merge tags: `{field:name}`, `{all_fields}`, `{form:title}`, `{submission:id}`, `{submission:url}`, `{submission:date}`, `{user:email}`, `{user:name}`, `{site:title}`, `{site:url}`, `{admin_email}` (`MERGE_TAGS`, `renderMergeTags`).

**Handling.** `cms.forms.list(form, { status, search, after, limit }, principal)`, `counts`, `inboxCounts`, `submission`, `setStatus`, `delete`, `setNote` and `csv` (an async iterator of CSV text with formula cells defused); `cms.forms.maintain()` empties old trash. The scaffold places forms with the `core/form` block (`FormView` on `RenderedBlock.form`, `InputView` on each input), posts to `POST /api/cms/forms/<slug>` with or without JavaScript, and adds Forms, the submissions inbox and CSV export to the dashboard.

guides.title: Build field groups: meta boxes from blocks, with repeaters
guides.summary: Field groups lay typed fields out with blocks and attach to collections, taxonomies, users and menu items; field blocks compile to declarations, rows fields are repeaters with derived indexed lists, conditions hide fields on write, and targets without documents carry meta.
guides.markdown:
**Field groups are meta boxes built from blocks.** A `FieldGroup` is `{ id, title, description?, placement?, order?, targets, blocks }`: `targets` lists where its box shows (`{ kind: 'collection', name }`, `{ kind: 'taxonomy', name }`, `{ kind: 'users' }`, `{ kind: 'menus' }`), and `blocks` is a tree of *field blocks* (`field/text`, `field/number`, `field/choice`, `field/media`, `field/reference`, `field/blocks`, `field/repeater`, …; `FIELD_BLOCKS`, one per `FIELD_BLOCK_TYPES` entry) laid out with the core layout blocks (`FIELD_GROUP_LAYOUT`: group, columns, grid, tabs, heading, paragraph as a note, divider). A field block's data is the builder's field settings: `label`, `name` (from the label when empty, as `inputName`), `description`, `required`, `width`, and per kind `max`, `min`, `unique`, `index` (filterable), `search`, `choices`, `defaultValue`, `target`, `blocks`. `validateBlocks(blocks, types, { fieldGroup: { scope } })` checks a group's tree: only field and layout blocks, names distinct across the group (rows included) and never one of `scope` (the target's own fields), conditions (`Block.when`, the form builder's rules) naming fields in reach.

**Groups compile to declarations.** `fieldGroupDeclarations(blocks, types)` turns the tree into `{ [name]: FieldDeclaration }`: layout contributes what it holds, a repeater becomes a `rows` field whose `fields` are its children. The host merges a target's groups into its resource (`cms.resourceById('cms/products').fields` holds the group's fields), so storage, the API, search and themes see fields and never layout. Values are stored flat by name. A collection's own fields are its first group: `CollectionDefinition.layout` holds the builder's tree and `saveCollection` compiles `fields` from it; a definition without `layout` gets `layoutOf(fields)`.

**Rows.** `field.rows({ name: field.string({ required: true }), notes: field.rows({ … }) }, { max: 20 })` declares a repeater: a list of at most `max` rows (`ROW_LIMITS`), each an object of its fields with an `_id` the host assigns when missing (`withRowIds`); rows nest without limit. `validateValue` walks rows; `unique` on a row field holds within the record (`rowUniqueProblem`); `search` on a row field adds its text to the record's search text (`rowsPlain`, `rowsSearchable`). A row field with `index` or `unique` makes the host keep a derived list beside the document: `derivedFields(fields)` names it `specs__name` (`derivedName(['specs', 'name'])`) with `derived: ['specs', 'name']` and an array index, filled with the distinct values at that path across every row (`derivedValues`). Derived fields are never written by clients nor returned; `repository.list({ where: { 'specs.name': { contains: 'Weight' } } })` seeks through them. Ranges and sorting on row fields are not offered.

**Conditions on fields.** `fieldVisibility(blocks, types, values, scope)` returns the `hiddenKey`s of the blocks the conditions hide and the values with hidden fields cleared, rows included: a row's field sees the row's values over the rows above over the top level, and hidden fields count as empty. The repository runs it on every write with the record as it would be, so a hidden required field is not required and a hidden value is stored as null; editors run it on each change.

**Targets without documents.** Terms, users and menu items carry `meta`: `taxonomies.create(taxonomy, { name, meta })`, `users.update(id, { meta })` and `MenuItem.meta` are checked against the target's groups by `metaProblems(fields, meta, next)` through the host (`fieldVisibility` included); `TermShape.meta`, `CmsUser.meta` and `MenuItemView.meta` return them. Host step 10 adds `cms_field_groups` and the `meta` columns.

**Host API.** `cms.fieldGroups.all()`, `.get(id)`, `.forTarget(target)`; `cms.fieldGroupsFor(target)` (the loaded groups); `cms.saveFieldGroup(group, principal)` (checks the tree against the block types and each target's fields, keeps names distinct across a target's groups, stores the group and plans the targets' schemas: new indexes come, dropped fields keep their values); `cms.deleteFieldGroup(id, principal)`. Permission `cms:collections`. The dashboard's `/dashboard/field-groups` screens, the collection builder's layout tree, the entry editor's boxes with repeater rows, the term editor and the menu item's Fields tab use them; the content API filters with `?filter[specs.name]=Weight`.
